name: Icon
purpose: Communicates meaning, action, or status through a recognizable visual symbol. Always supplemental to text — never the sole conveyor of information without a tooltip or label.
neverUseFor: Decorative illustration — use an Illustration component instead
Brand logomarks — use Image or dedicated Logo component
Animated icons — Tabler outline icons are static; wrap in a motion component if animation is needed
rationale: Every Tabler icon renders through Icon so size, stroke, color and aria-hidden are decided once instead of at each call site, which is how components drifted before. Stroke is derived from size by the stroke rule (ADR-017), the icon set is swappable (ADR-014), and Icon is always supplemental to text — accessibility lives at the usage site.

mayExtendLocally: Pick any Tabler icon component reference for a given usage
Choose a size from the documented scale and an icon-* color token
mustEscalateToDS: Passing stroke to change icon weight (edit ICON_STROKE_PX_BY_SIZE instead)
Rendering a raw <IconXxx> outside the Icon component
Adding new sizes, custom SVG sets or animated icons

tablerOfficialStroke.note: Tabler default. Goes on the root <svg> ONLY — never on <path> children. Configurable via CSS.

helixStrokeRule.unit: Line width as seen on screen, in CSS px. The SVG stroke attribute is converted from this in code (iconStrokeForSize) — never documented or edited by hand.
rules: Icon applies the rule automatically — never pass stroke at a call site to make an icon heavier or lighter.
To change icon weight system-wide, edit ICON_STROKE_PX_BY_SIZE (and this block + ADR-017), nothing else.
Real px must never decrease as size grows — each rung is at least as thick as the one below it.

Line weight grows faster as icons get larger: +0.1px per step up to 24px, +0.2px per 4px from 24 to 36, +0.4px from 36 to 40 — large icons need visibly heavier lines to hold their presence. Sizes between rungs interpolate real px linearly; outside 12–40 the edge rung's svg stroke is held.
A deliberate one-off override (e.g. Checkbox's stroke={3} checkmark) must be at least as thick as the rule at that size, and commented at the call site.

mustFollow: Only <path> elements inside SVG — no <circle>, <rect>, <ellipse>, <line>, <polygon>, <polyline>, <g>. Convert everything to path.
stroke-width goes on root <svg> only — never on child <path> elements
fill=none on outline icons — stroke only, never filled areas
stroke=currentColor on root <svg> — never hardcode a color
No closing Z on outline icon paths (Tabler removes it via optimizer)
Optical weight must match Tabler icons at 24px with stroke-width=2
Minimum path detail: legible at 16×16px (smallest Helix usage size)
Naming in Figma: PascalCase, no prefix — 'HeartCustom' (matching Tabler's bare-name convention)
SVG file metadata comment: tags, category (one of the 41 official), version, unicode
Every outline icon may optionally have a matching filled variant in icons/filled/
mustNot: Use stroke-width on <path> elements — only on root <svg>
Add fills or gradients to outline icons
Use sharp corners (linecap: butt, linejoin: miter) — always round
Include Z/z close-path on outline icon paths
Include title or desc SVG elements — accessibility is the usage site's responsibility
Use more than 3 path elements — simpler is better; complex icons suggest wrong category
referenceIcons: IconPlus — simplest form: 2 paths (vertical + horizontal line)
IconAlertCircle — 3 paths: circle arc + exclamation body + dot (h.01 trick with round linecap)
IconSearch — 2 paths: circle arc + handle line

sizes.system: fixed values — never scale with CSS font-size

values.12: xs contexts — dense UI, inline badges
values.16: default — button slots, form elements, inline text, Input size=m
values.20: medium emphasis — card headers, section labels
values.24: large — native icon size, icon-only buttons, empty states
values.40: xxxlarge — largest icon size, same use as 36

sizes.note: Icon components always render at the size passed via the size prop. The Figma component is 24×24 (native grid); resize the instance at usage site.

colorRules.principle: Icons use their own icon/* semantic tokens, set explicitly — never inherited from a text/* token, even when the resolved color happens to match
colorRules.standalone: Use icon/neutral or icon/neutral-light — never text/* tokens, never primitives
colorRules.forbidden: Never hardcode hex values. Never reference a text/* token for icon color. Never use primitive color scales directly.

anatomy.description: SVG element with viewBox='0 0 24 24'. Never add a wrapper div.

anatomy.element: path (or g > path for compound icons)
anatomy.description: The drawn artwork. stroke=currentColor, fill=none, stroke-width derived from size by the ADR-017 stroke rule (see iconStyle.helixStrokeRule). Generated inside the Tabler icon component — not addressable as a data-helix-part from the Helix Icon wrapper; only icon-root carries the attribute.

props.name: icon
props.description: The icon component to render, passed by reference (e.g. IconPlus), not by name string. Defaults to Tabler's outline set, but accepts any component matching the size/stroke/color/SVG-passthrough shape (see interop note below) — not a Tabler-only prop.

props.name: stroke
props.description: Stroke width applied to the icon path. Defaults to the ADR-017 stroke rule for the rendered size (see iconStyle.helixStrokeRule) — don't pass it to adjust weight; only for a deliberate, commented one-off.

props.name: color
props.description: Icon stroke color. Prefer inherited currentColor.

props.name: decorative
props.description: Marks the icon as decorative when a visible label already exists.

props.name: className
props.description: Additional className for the root svg.

figma.layout: Flat grid — COMPONENT nodes directly on page,  no row frames
figma.codeOnly: Icon is a code-only wrapper (owner's decision 2026-10-21,  option A): in code it sets the size,  derives the stroke weight from it (ADR-017) and handles color and aria; in Figma every component already places its icon instance at the right size and stroke per variant,  so there is nothing for an Icon set to add. Designers use the icon components on the Icons page directly. A loose icon scaled by hand in Figma does not re-derive its stroke like code does — pick the size from the icon component,  don't scale it.

icon.reason: code-only wrapper: Figma swaps the icon on the consuming component (iconSwap),  never on an Icon set

size.reason: code-only wrapper: each component variant already draws its icon at the size and stroke ADR-017 gives that size

Default.reason: Icon has no component set with properties — icons are the Icons page (icons-to-figma)

IconOnly.reason: Icon has no component set with properties — icons are the Icons page (icons-to-figma)

Sizes.reason: Icon has no component set with properties — icons are the Icons page (icons-to-figma)

Colors.reason: Icon has no component set with properties — icons are the Icons page (icons-to-figma)

CustomIconSet.reason: Icon has no component set with properties — icons are the Icons page (icons-to-figma)

InlineWithText.reason: Icon has no component set with properties — icons are the Icons page (icons-to-figma)

interop.note: Icon is icon-set-agnostic by type (ADR-014) — Tabler is the documented default, not a hard requirement. Any component matching HelixIconComponent's shape (size/stroke/color + standard SVG props) can be passed directly to icon/iconEnd on any Helix component. Sets with a different prop dialect (e.g. Lucide's strokeWidth) can be wrapped with createIconAdapter from packages/core/src/components/Icon/createIconAdapter.ts before being passed.

a11y.aria: aria-hidden='true' when accompanied by a visible label. aria-label='Description' when icon-only.
a11y.note: The icon component itself renders aria-hidden. Accessibility is the responsibility of the usage site.

motion: CSS transitions/animations: neutralised by the global prefers-reduced-motion rule

createCustomIcon: 2. Sketch paths on 24×24 grid, stroke-width=1.8 (the ADR-017 rule at 24px), rounded caps
3. Export SVG — extract the path d= attribute
6. Run icons-to-figma skill Step 2–4 for the new icon
7. Verify: renders clearly at 16×16, stroke weight matches IconPlus at same size
